title: Gone-Greek Spinach Risotto
subtitle: with Roasted Cannellini Beans and Vegan Feta
description: It’s plant power all the way with our super-tasty vegan dishes! Our meat-free, dairy-free, honey-free dishes are amped with plant-based proteins, fresh produce, nuts and seeds. Best of all, they’re for everyone, whether you're vegan, vegetarian or flexitarian.

steps.text: Roast cannellini beans: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Drain and rinse half the cannellini beans, then pat dry with paper towel. Put the beans on the lined tray, drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil and toss to coat. Roast for 20 mins or until golden and crisp. Season with salt and pepper.

Start risotto: Meanwhile, crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Finely chop the onion. Trim the green beans and halve on an angle. Coarsely chop the olives (see Make it yours). Heat 1 tbs olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the garlic and onion, stirring, for 3-4 mins until softened. Add the rice and cook, stirring, for 1-2 mins until the grains are well coated.

Finish risotto: Stir the Greek seasoning and 310ml (1¼ cups) boiling water into the rice, reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, for 15 mins or until most of the liquid is absorbed and the rice is almost tender. Add the spinach and 2 tbs boiling water and stir to combine. Remove the pan from the heat and stand, covered, for 5 mins.
Cook green beans: While the risotto is cooking, bring a small saucepan of water to the boil. Add the green beans to the pan and cook for 3 mins or until tender. Drain.

Serve up: Stir the green beans into the risotto. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the risotto among bowls, scatter with the roasted cannellini beans and olives and crumble over the vegan feta. Enjoy!

Make it yours: We love the salty pops of flavour that the olives provide, but if some members of your family aren't keen on them, then use less or none at all. Or keep everyone happy and serve them on the side!
